crop.notes: Whole article, headline to 'FINALLY, AND TO CONCLUDE.' A fold or overlapping scrap in crop-2 hides the right edge of several lines in the Gallagher paragraph (e.g. 'He st[ruck] Tom Allen under the left ear'), but the article is otherwise complete.

ocr.notes: Mostly right. Drops the sub-heads (the first call was at 'M'COOLE'S own saloon', not 'a saloon'); 'He faced Tom Allen' should be about 'He struck'; 'arbiter' is 'manager'; 'Jack Loosey' is 'Jack Looney'; 'fistic' omitted before 'preliminaries'. Words in the fold-hidden lines are reconstructed.

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican toured St. Louis sporting saloons, including McCoole's and Allen's Concert Saloon on Fifth Street, on the eve of the Allen–McCoole fight and found little excitement; Allen was said to be waiting at Venice.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Missouri Republican—St. Louis, June 15, [1]869' (first digit cut). Article is at the top of the sixth column.

facts.fact: On the eve of the McCoole fight, Allen's Concert Saloon on Fifth Street between O'Fallon and Biddle was crowded for a 'Free and Easy' night, mostly with Englishmen; a photograph of Allen hung over the bar
places: Tom Allen's Concert Saloon, Fifth Street between O'Fallon and Biddle, St. Louis

facts.fact: On the night before the McCoole fight Allen was away from St. Louis, reportedly at Venice (the paper jokes about a 'steam gondola' to carry him to the battle)
Carroll, of Carroll's Dramatic Saloon near the Varieties, was understood to have been the go-between through whom Allen and McCoole arranged their match
places: Carroll's Dramatic Saloon, near the Varieties, St. Louis

notes: 'Venice' is a humorous reference; Venice, Illinois, across the river, is the likely meaning but the article does not say so. The Gallagher paragraph recalls his blow under Allen's left ear in their earlier fight; left out of the facts as already covered by the fight record.
